evals.prompt: hey I just finished the login form validation, commit and push it up so the team can see it
evals.expected_output: Stages changed files, generates a conventional commit message (e.g. feat: add login form validation), commits, and pushes to the remote tracking branch. Reports commit SHA and remote ref.
expectations: stages changed files using explicit file paths, not git add -A or git add .
generates a conventional commit message with an appropriate type prefix (feat:, fix:, etc.)
commit message subject line is under 70 characters
pushes to the current branch's remote tracking branch
does NOT include any AI attribution lines like Co-Authored-By in the commit

evals.expected_output: Recognizes 'ship it' as a commit-and-push intent. Analyzes the diff, stages files, generates a conventional commit message, and pushes to the upstream branch.
expectations: recognizes 'ship it' as a commit-and-push intent triggering the cp skill
runs git diff to analyze the actual changes before generating a message
generates a meaningful conventional commit message from the diff, not a generic message like 'update files'
pushes to the current branch's upstream remote

evals.prompt: push my changes to remote, I fixed the null pointer exception in the webhook handler
evals.expected_output: Commits the webhook handler fix with a fix: type conventional commit message and pushes to origin.
expectations: uses fix: as the conventional commit type since the user described a bug fix
commit message references the webhook handler or null pointer fix
commits any uncommitted work before pushing
does NOT create a pull request, only pushes

evals.prompt: commit and push everything, I've been working on models and also patched that API rate limiter bug
evals.expected_output: Analyzes the diff to identify logically separate changes. Creates separate commits for the new models (feat:) and the bug fix (fix:), then pushes all commits in a single push.
expectations: analyzes the diff to identify logically separate changes (new models vs bug fix)
creates separate commits with appropriate types: feat: for new models, fix: for the bug fix
pushes all commits to remote in a single push operation
stages files using explicit paths, not git add -A

evals.prompt: cp everything, make sure nothing sensitive gets in there - I have a .env.local and some new config files
evals.expected_output: Excludes .env.local and any other sensitive files from staging. Warns the user about skipped confidential files. Stages and commits only non-sensitive files, then pushes.
expectations: excludes .env.local from staging
checks for and excludes other confidential files like credentials.json, *.key, *.pem
warns the user about which confidential files were skipped
stages only non-sensitive files for commit
does NOT silently include secrets in the commit

evals.prompt: /cp "fix: resolve race condition in session middleware"
evals.expected_output: Uses the provided commit message verbatim instead of auto-generating one. Stages changes, commits with the exact message, and pushes.
expectations: uses the provided commit message verbatim: 'fix: resolve race condition in session middleware'
does not auto-generate or modify the provided commit message
stages and commits the changes
pushes to the remote tracking branch

evals.prompt: I updated the .claude/commands/deploy.md file with better instructions, ship it
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the .claude/ directory special commit rules. Uses perf: type for modified .claude/ markdown files, not docs:. Commits and pushes.
expectations: uses perf: as the commit type for modified .claude/ markdown files, not docs:
commit message references the updated deploy command or instructions
does NOT include AI attribution lines in the commit
pushes the commit to remote

evals.prompt: send it up, the branch doesn't have an upstream yet - it's feat/oauth-flow
evals.expected_output: Detects no upstream tracking branch. Stages, commits, and pushes using git push -u origin feat/oauth-flow to set the upstream.
expectations: detects that the branch has no upstream tracking branch
uses git push -u origin to set the upstream on first push
generates a conventional commit message from the diff
reports success with the remote ref after push
